tasks.title: Magnetic dock hover on card rows (StoryCard, SeriesCard, ChapterList row, ContinueCard)
tasks.useCase: Card lists react to the cursor like a Mac OS dock — the card under the pointer (and its neighbors) scale + lift toward the cursor, falling back to rest as the pointer moves away. Applied on the homepage hero card list, the /browse and /search CardGrid, the ContinueReadingRow card strip, and the chapter list rows on /series/[id].
tasks.gsapPlugin: core (gsap.quickTo + gsap.utils.mapRange) — no extra plugin required, just gsap.to with overwrite:auto and gsap.quickTo for the per-frame x/y/scale setters
tasks.demoReference: https://gsap.com/demos/ (magnetic-effect / dock-style hover pattern — uses gsap.quickTo + pointermove distance mapping)
tasks.approach: Add a single shared client hook useMagneticDock({ radius: 200, maxScale: 1.4, maxLift: 12 }) that scopes itself to a container ref, queries [data-dock-item] children, and on pointermove on the container maps each item's center-distance from the cursor through gsap.utils.mapRange(0..200, [1.4,1]) for scale and (0..200, [12,0]) for translateY. Uses gsap.quickTo per item for x/y/scale to avoid per-tween allocation. On pointerleave the hook tweens every item back to {scale:1, y:0, duration:0.45, ease:'power3.out'}. Each card component receives data-dock-item on its root anchor: SeriesCard <Link>, StoryCard <Link>, ContinueCard <Link>, and ChapterList's <Link className={styles.row}> in frontend/app/series/[id]/_components/ChapterList.tsx (line 84). Because frontend/app/page.tsx is a server component exporting metadata, the home hero card list cannot host the pointermove hook directly — a new client wrapper frontend/app/_components/HeroCardsList.tsx wraps the existing <SeriesCard> map in a div that mounts the hook. The hook's reduced-motion path no-ops the listener entirely. To prevent CSS hover transforms from fighting GSAP, the rule .card:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); ... } at frontend/components/ContinueReadingRow.module.css lines 67-70 is removed, and the transform leg of the transition at lines 63-66 is removed (border-color transition stays). Same pass on .row:hover and the .row transition rules in ChapterList.module.css and equivalent rules in StoryCard.module.css / SeriesCard CSS. NOT in scope: /tag/[slug] (its layout doesn't share the dock container), admin lists, the search filter pills.
tasks.githubIssueBody:
## What
Add a Mac-style magnetic dock hover effect to card rows so the card under the cursor (and its near neighbors) scale up and lift toward the pointer.

## Why
Card rows on /, /browse, /search, /series/[id], and the ContinueReadingRow currently use a static CSS transform on :hover. A magnetic dock makes the entire row feel responsive to the cursor and reinforces "this is a curated catalog you can browse" — at the cost of one shared hook.

## Scope
- New hook: `frontend/lib/useMagneticDock.ts`
- New client wrapper: `frontend/app/_components/HeroCardsList.tsx` (because `frontend/app/page.tsx` is a server component that exports `metadata` — it cannot host pointermove listeners)
- Add `data-dock-item` to the link root of: SeriesCard, StoryCard, ContinueCard, and the `<Link className={styles.row}>` chapter row at `frontend/app/series/[id]/_components/ChapterList.tsx:84`
- Mount the hook in: CardGrid, ContinueReadingRow, HeroCardsList, ChapterList

## Tuning numbers (DO NOT change without design review)
- `radius: 200` (px from cursor — falloff distance)
- `maxScale: 1.4` (item directly under cursor)
- `maxLift: 12` (px translateY toward viewport top)
- Falloff: linear via `gsap.utils.mapRange(0, 200, max, 1)`; clamp at >= 1
- Settle tween on pointerleave: `duration: 0.45, ease: 'power3.out'`

## CSS cleanup (REQUIRED)
The existing CSS `:hover` transforms will fight GSAP's quickTo writes. Remove these specific rules:
- `frontend/components/ContinueReadingRow.module.css`: delete `transform var(--transition-fast),` from the multi-property `transition:` block at lines 63-66; delete the `transform: translateY(-2px);` line from `.card:hover` at lines 67-70 (keep `border-color`)
- `frontend/app/series/[id]/_components/ChapterList.module.css`: remove the transform leg of any `transition:` block on `.row` and any `:hover` rule that sets `transform`
- Same pass on `StoryCard.module.css`, `SeriesCard` styles, and `ContinueCard.module.css`

## Out of scope
- `/tag/[slug]` (separate layout, no shared dock container)
- Admin lists
- TagBar pills / search filter chips

## Reduced motion
`prefersReducedMotion()` causes the hook to bail before attaching any pointer listener — items stay at rest.

## Test plan

- [ ] Hover /browse CardGrid — same dock feel
- [ ] Hover ContinueReadingRow on chapter page — same
- [ ] Hover ChapterList row on /series/[id] — same
- [ ] Toggle macOS reduce-motion — hook no-ops, no transform applied
- [ ] Keyboard-tab through cards — focus ring intact, no transform applied (pointermove only)
- [ ] Rapid pointer flick across the row — no tween stacking (overwrite:auto)
- [ ] DevTools throttle to 4x CPU — verify quickTo keeps up at 60fps

tasks.title: FLIP-based expand/collapse for admin NoteCard inside NotesPanel
tasks.useCase: Each admin NoteCard expands from a small pill to a full-height composer card. Today the panel uses a CSS max-height transition; this swaps in GSAP Flip so the expanding card morphs from its pill rect to its open rect (with siblings yielding via absolute:true), eliminating the layout pop when the textarea height is unknown.
tasks.approach: Inside NotesPanel.tsx, on the moment the active note id changes, capture Flip.getState() for every .card descendant BEFORE setState (using a useLayoutEffect+ref trick or by snapshotting in the click handler immediately before the React state update). After commit, useGSAP({ scope: panelRef, dependencies: [activeId] }) calls Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.45, ease: 'power2.inOut', absolute: true, simple: true, nested: true, onEnter: els => gsap.from(els, { autoAlpha: 0, duration: 0.25 }) }). Mount strategy: ALWAYS render both branches — pill markup and expanded markup live in the same component tree gated by `expanded`, and the children persist across the toggle so Flip can match them by node identity. Stray autosaves on collapsed cards are gated by a debounce that checks `expanded` synchronously inside the autosave handler (drop the write if not expanded). The per-card `transition: transform 180ms, ... box-shadow 220ms` at NoteCard.module.css lines 18-22 is REMOVED for the `transform` leg only (keep border-color / box-shadow); GSAP owns transform via Flip + T1's dock writes. To reconcile T1's dock writes with Flip, all Flip.from tweens use `overwrite: 'auto'`. The panel-level `transition: max-height 260ms` at NotesPanel.module.css lines 28-31 is REMOVED on `.panel.hasExpanded` because Flip animates the expanded card's rect itself; the panel just resizes to fit. Reduced-motion path skips Flip.from entirely and sets `overflow: hidden` on the panel while open===false so the collapsed pills don't leak content during the synchronous swap. Register Flip in frontend/lib/gsap.ts.
tasks.githubIssueBody:
## What
Replace the CSS max-height transition on admin NoteCard expand/collapse with a GSAP Flip morph so the card transitions from its pill rect to its open rect with siblings yielding cleanly.

## Why
The current `transition: max-height 260ms` on `.panel.hasExpanded` (NotesPanel.module.css:28-31) can't smoothly handle the textarea's unknown intrinsic height; you see a pop on expand and a snap on collapse. Flip captures both rects and tweens between them.

## Approach (committed)
- **Mount strategy**: always render both pill + expanded markup inside the same component subtree (do NOT unmount on collapse). Children persist by ref so Flip can match them.
- **Autosave guard**: the textarea autosave handler checks `expanded` synchronously and drops the write if false (defends against the always-mounted collapsed branch firing autosaves).
- **CSS coordination**:
  - REMOVE the `transform` leg of the `transition:` block at `NoteCard.module.css:18-22` (keep border-color, box-shadow)
  - REMOVE `max-height 260ms ...` from the `transition:` block at `NotesPanel.module.css:28-31` on `.panel` (Flip animates the cards; the panel just resizes to fit)
  - Use `overwrite: 'auto'` on every Flip.from tween so T1's dock writes don't fight
- **Reduced motion**: skip Flip.from and instead toggle classes synchronously; set `overflow: hidden` on the panel when `open === false` so collapsed pills don't visually overflow during the swap
- **gsap.ts**: register Flip alongside existing ScrollTrigger — single `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, Flip)` call (see cross-cutting note in T4/T5)

## Files
- `frontend/app/admin/_components/NoteCard.tsx`
- `frontend/app/admin/_components/NoteCard.module.css`
- `frontend/app/admin/_components/NotesPanel.tsx`
- `frontend/app/admin/_components/NotesPanel.module.css`
- `frontend/lib/gsap.ts`

## Test plan
- [ ] /admin → open a note card — pill morphs to full-height composer
- [ ] Collapse it — full-height morphs back to pill, no max-height pop
- [ ] Open one, then click another — first collapses while second opens in one timeline
- [ ] Hover other note cards during expand — T1 dock effect doesn't fight Flip's transform
- [ ] Toggle reduce-motion — no animation, no overflow leak, autosave still works
- [ ] Edit textarea, collapse, expand — content preserved (proves persistent mount)
tasks.reducedMotionPlan: When prefersReducedMotion() is true, the Flip.from call is skipped entirely — the React commit synchronously swaps DOM classes/sizes. To prevent the always-mounted collapsed markup from visually leaking during the synchronous swap, `.panel:not(.hasExpanded) .card` gets `overflow: hidden`. Border-color hover stays via CSS.
tasks.changesFromOriginal: Added NotesPanel.module.css to filesToChange and reconciled the panel-level `transition: max-height 260ms` (lines 28-31) with the per-card Flip — it must be removed because Flip owns the size animation. Committed to the always-render-both-branches mount strategy with an autosave guard (the alternative — useLayoutEffect-on-mount measure — was harder to reconcile with autosave). Specified that the reduced-motion path must set `overflow: hidden` on collapsed panels. Called out the NoteCard `.card transition: transform 180ms` rule (lines 18-22) and committed to removing the transform leg while keeping overwrite:'auto' on Flip + T1's dock for safety.

tasks.title: Physics-based click feedback for Like / Save / Share / QuoteShare buttons
tasks.useCase: Like / Save / Share / QuoteShare buttons feel tactile on press: a CustomBounce squish-and-rebound on the button itself, a per-button color flash via box-shadow, and (Like only) a Physics2DPlugin confetti burst spawning short-lived particle spans. All three layers run on one timeline.

It (a) tweens scale 0.86→1 with CustomBounce.create('btnBounce', { strength:0.55, squash:1.4 }), (b) flashes a box-shadow directly via gsap.fromTo(el, { boxShadow: `0 0 0 0 ${flashColor}` }, { boxShadow: `0 0 0 12px ${flashColor}00`, duration: 0.55 }) — chose direct box-shadow over CSS variables so no @property registration is needed and Safari/older browsers get smooth interpolation, (c) on burst:true, spawns 14 fixed-position 6px spans at the button's center and tweens each with physics2D:{ velocity:gsap.utils.random(260,420), angle:gsap.utils.random(-110,-70), gravity:900, friction:0.06 }, removed onComplete. Wiring per button: LikeButton already has buttonRef + useGSAP({ scope: buttonRef }); add the pressFeedback(buttonRef.current!, '#ff3860', true) call inside the existing onClick toggle. SaveButton + ShareButton: add `const buttonRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)`, attach `ref={buttonRef}`, wrap effects with `useGSAP({ scope: buttonRef })`, and call pressFeedback(buttonRef.current!, 'var(--gold)', false) [Save] / pressFeedback(buttonRef.current!, 'var(--text-muted)', false) [Share]. **--text-muted is already defined in frontend/app/globals.css at line 144 — no new color token, no globals.css change.** QuoteShare integration (chosen approach): WIDEN the signature in frontend/components/QuoteShare.tsx line 170 from `onShareClick = async (target: ShareTarget, index: number)` to `onShareClick = async (target: ShareTarget, index: number, e?: React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>)` and at line 217 change the onClick to `onClick={(e) => void onShareClick(target, i, e)}`. Inside onShareClick, if `e?.currentTarget` is present, call pressFeedback(e.currentTarget, 'var(--gold)', false). Rejected the ref-per-button alternative (an array of refs synced to the share targets array adds churn that the event-arg path avoids). Register Physics2DPlugin, CustomBounce, CustomEase in frontend/lib/gsap.ts.
tasks.githubIssueBody:
## What
Add tactile, physics-based click feedback to every primary action button: Like, Save, Share, and each per-target button inside QuoteShare. CustomBounce on the scale, box-shadow flash, optional Physics2D confetti burst on Like.

## Approach (committed decisions)

**Flash color mechanism — direct box-shadow tween** (NOT a CSS custom property). GSAP can interpolate `box-shadow` strings directly, so we sidestep needing `@property --pulse-flash` in globals.css and we get correct interpolation on older Safari.

**Per-button refs + useGSAP scope** — explicitly required for ALL three buttons, not just LikeButton (LikeButton already has it at line 17/44):
- `SaveButton.tsx`: add `const buttonRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)`, attach `ref={buttonRef}`, wrap with `useGSAP({ scope: buttonRef })`, call `pressFeedback(buttonRef.current!, 'var(--gold)', false)` in onClick
- `ShareButton.tsx`: same pattern with `pressFeedback(buttonRef.current!, 'var(--text-muted)', false)`

**ShareButton flash color = `var(--text-muted)`** (already defined in `frontend/app/globals.css:144`). globals.css is NOT in filesToChange — no new color token needed.

**QuoteShare integration — widen the onClick signature** (NOT ref-per-button). Current state, verified:
- `frontend/components/QuoteShare.tsx:170` is `const onShareClick = async (target: ShareTarget, index: number) => { ... }` — no event arg
- `frontend/components/QuoteShare.tsx:217` is `onClick={() => void onShareClick(target, i)}`

Change to:
- `const onShareClick = async (target: ShareTarget, index: number, e?: React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => { ... }`
- `onClick={(e) => void onShareClick(target, i, e)}`
- Inside the handler, when `e?.currentTarget` exists, call `pressFeedback(e.currentTarget, 'var(--gold)', false)`.

Rejected alternative: an array of refs synced to the targets array. The event-arg path is shorter and matches the existing pattern in the file.

## Files
- New: `frontend/lib/pressFeedback.ts`
- Modified: `LikeButton.tsx`, `SaveButton.tsx`, `ShareButton.tsx`, `QuoteShare.tsx` and their module.css siblings (only if a `transform-origin` tweak is needed)
- `frontend/lib/gsap.ts` — register Physics2DPlugin + CustomBounce + CustomEase

## Tuning
- CustomBounce: `strength: 0.55, squash: 1.4, endAtStart: false`
- Scale fromTo: `0.86 → 1` over 0.9s ease 'btnBounce'
- Box-shadow flash: 0→12px outset, 0.55s, color = `flashColor` then alpha 0
- Like burst: 14 particles, velocity 260-420, angle -110..-70, gravity 900, friction 0.06

## Reduced motion
When `prefersReducedMotion()` is true, pressFeedback skips the bounce + burst entirely and instead tweens box-shadow to a steady 0.85 alpha for 120ms then back. Color feedback remains, motion does not.

## Test plan
- [ ] Tap Like — squish + rebound, confetti burst, button settles
- [ ] Tap Save — squish + rebound, gold box-shadow flash, no particles
- [ ] Tap Share — squish + rebound, muted box-shadow flash, no particles
- [ ] Open QuoteShare, tap each share target — squish + gold flash per button
- [ ] Keyboard activate (Space/Enter) on each — same feedback (event still has currentTarget)
- [ ] Rapid double-tap — second tween overwrites first (overwrite:'auto'), no stacking
- [ ] Toggle reduce-motion — only the steady box-shadow pulse fires; no bounce/burst/squish
- [ ] Verify Physics2DPlugin loads in free GSAP — `gsap.registerPlugin` does not throw
tasks.reducedMotionPlan: pressFeedback's first line checks prefersReducedMotion(). When true: skip CustomBounce, skip particles, just gsap.fromTo(el, { boxShadow: `0 0 0 0 ${flashColor}` }, { boxShadow: `0 0 0 6px ${flashColor}00`, duration: 0.12 }). Color feedback remains.
tasks.changesFromOriginal: Swapped the elastic/back.out ease for the physics-based-effects demo (CustomBounce + Physics2DPlugin). Dropped the CSS custom-property pulse trick in favor of tweening box-shadow directly — no @property registration in globals.css needed. Confirmed by reading frontend/components/QuoteShare.tsx that onShareClick (line 170) takes (target, index) with NO event; committed to widening the signature and adding e?.currentTarget rather than the ref-array alternative. Made the useRef + useGSAP({ scope: buttonRef }) setup explicit for SaveButton AND ShareButton (LikeButton already has it). Pinned ShareButton's flash to `var(--text-muted)` (defined at globals.css:144) so globals.css is NOT in filesToChange.

tasks.title: Smooth scroll restore using ScrollToPlugin in useReadingPosition
tasks.useCase: When a returning visitor reopens a chapter they've already started, the page glides them back to their saved scroll position instead of jumping. Driven by a swap at frontend/lib/useReadingPosition.ts line 119 from `window.scrollTo({ top, behavior: 'instant' })` to a GSAP ScrollToPlugin tween, with auto-kill so any user input instantly cancels the restore.
tasks.approach: Register ScrollToPlugin in frontend/lib/gsap.ts alongside existing ScrollTrigger (single call: `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, ScrollToPlugin)`). In useReadingPosition.ts, replace the `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })` at line 119 with a branch: if `window.location.hash` is non-empty (especially `#:~:text=` text-fragment links) OR `prefersReducedMotion()` is true, KEEP the instant jump (hash precedence rule). Otherwise run `gsap.to(window, { scrollTo: { y: target, autoKill: true }, duration: 1.1, ease: 'power2.out', overwrite: 'auto', onUpdate: () => ScrollTrigger.update(), onAutoKill: () => { restoringRef.current = false }, onComplete: () => { restoringRef.current = false }, onInterrupt: () => { restoringRef.current = false } })`. Tween storage: add `const tweenRef = useRef<gsap.core.Tween | null>(null)` in the hook; assign the tween to tweenRef.current and call tweenRef.current?.kill() in the existing cleanup return. Pause the write throttler during restore: add `const restoringRef = useRef(false)`, set it `true` immediately before launching the tween (and on the synchronous instant-jump branch too, for parity); inside onScroll, early-return `if (restoringRef.current) return;` so the programmatic scroll never triggers PATCHes. autoKill clears restoringRef via the three callbacks. Duration/ease pinned: 1.1s power2.out (no distance-aware scaling).
tasks.githubIssueBody:
## What
Replace the instant `window.scrollTo` at `frontend/lib/useReadingPosition.ts:119` with a GSAP `ScrollToPlugin` tween so returning readers glide back to their saved position.

## Decisions (committed)
- **Duration**: 1.1s fixed, no distance-aware scaling
- **Ease**: `power2.out`
- **autoKill**: `true` (default for window targets — any user wheel/touch/key input cancels the tween instantly, which is the whole point)
- **Hash precedence**: ANY non-empty `window.location.hash` — especially text fragments like `#:~:text=...` — wins; skip the tween and let the browser handle the anchor/fragment
- **Reduced motion**: skip the tween, retain the existing `behavior: 'instant'` scrollTo
- **Tween storage**: `const tweenRef = useRef<gsap.core.Tween | null>(null)` so the existing cleanup return can `tweenRef.current?.kill()`
- **ScrollTrigger coordination**: pass `onUpdate: () => ScrollTrigger.update()` so any ScrollTrigger-driven reveals on the page fire correctly during the programmatic scroll
- **Write-throttle pause**: `const restoringRef = useRef(false)`; set true immediately before launching the tween; in `onScroll`, early-return when true; clear via `onAutoKill | onComplete | onInterrupt`. Prevents 100+ wasted PATCH calls during the 1.1s tween (the existing `WRITE_THROTTLE_MS = 5000` only kicks in after the first write)

## Files
- `frontend/lib/useReadingPosition.ts` (line 119 + surrounding effect)
- `frontend/lib/gsap.ts` (register ScrollToPlugin)

## Test plan
- [ ] Reopen /chapter/[id] mid-article — scroll glides to saved position in 1.1s with power2.out
- [ ] Flick the wheel mid-restore — tween aborts instantly (autoKill)
- [ ] Hit PageDown mid-restore — tween aborts (autoKill catches keyboard too)
- [ ] Open /chapter/[id]#some-heading — instant anchor jump, no tween
- [ ] Open /chapter/[id]#:~:text=hello — instant text-fragment scroll, no tween
- [ ] Toggle reduce-motion — instant restore, no tween
- [ ] Network tab — exactly 0 PATCH /reading-positions calls fired during the 1.1s tween (proves restoringRef guard)
- [ ] Unmount mid-tween (route change) — no console errors; tween cleaned via tweenRef.current?.kill()
tasks.reducedMotionPlan: If `prefersReducedMotion()` is true, retain the existing `window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: 'instant' })` branch unchanged. Animating ~1s of vertical scroll is a known vestibular trigger; the instant jump is the correct fallback. Note that even without reduce-motion, autoKill makes the tween instantly yield to any user keyboard/wheel/touch input, which is itself an a11y win.
tasks.changesFromOriginal: Pinned `tweenRef = useRef<gsap.core.Tween | null>(null)` so cleanup can kill the tween (matches existing cleanup return at line 202-214). Added `onUpdate: () => ScrollTrigger.update()` so ScrollTrigger reveals fire during the programmatic scroll. Added the `restoringRef` write-throttle pause so the tween itself doesn't trigger writes inside `onScroll` (the throttler doesn't otherwise gate the first write of a session). Pinned duration 1.1s + ease `power2.out` (no distance-aware variant). Committed to ANY non-empty `window.location.hash` (including `#:~:text=`) winning over the saved-position restore.

tasks.title: FLIP-based tag filter reflow on /search and /browse
tasks.useCase: Clicking a tag in TagBar on /search or /browse reflows the result grid with GSAP Flip so cards slide from their old slots to their new slots (and leavers fade out absolute-positioned without shoving siblings). Today the navigation full-replaces the card list with no animation.
tasks.approach: Because /search and /browse are server components that re-render the CardGrid on every URL change, the demo's pattern (Flip.getState before mutation, Flip.from after) does NOT survive across navigation — node refs are gone. Committed solution: a module-level FlipBridge in frontend/lib/flipBridge.ts that stashes a serialized Flip state keyed by the pathname + previous tagIds. TagBar's click handler (intercepted) calls bridge.snapshot(gsap.utils.toArray('[data-flip-id]')) synchronously before router.push, storing `Flip.getState(items, { props: 'opacity,transform' })` (state objects survive across renders because they hold cloned rects, not live nodes). On the next render, CardGrid mounts inside a useGSAP that pulls bridge.consume() and calls `Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.55, ease: 'power2.out', absolute: true, simple: true, stagger: { amount: 0.4 }, onEnter: els => gsap.fromTo(els, { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92 }, { opacity: 1, scale: 1, duration: 0.4 }), onLeave: els => gsap.to(els, { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92, duration: 0.3 }) })`. Suspense boundary: because the new client CardGrid reads useSearchParams, wrap CardGrid uses in `<Suspense fallback={<CardGrid.Skeleton />}>` inside frontend/app/search/page.tsx and frontend/app/browse/page.tsx. Card identity: every card carries `data-flip-id={`${type}:${id}`}` — added to StoryCard, SeriesCard, ContinueCard. ContinueCard.tsx and ContinueReadingRow.tsx are in scope because /search results can include continue-reading cards. Grid min-height: pin `min-height` on the .grid container at the start of Flip.from via a `gsap.set(container, { minHeight: container.offsetHeight })` and clear it onComplete — prevents the parent shrinking when leavers go absolute. Fast-Refresh safety: in flipBridge.ts add `if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && (module as any).hot) { (module as any).hot.dispose(() => bridge.clear()); }` plus an exported `bridge.clear()` callable. Document in a code comment that this is Webpack HMR API; the Next.js equivalent for Turbopack is `import.meta.webpackHot?.dispose?.(() => bridge.clear())`. Feature flag: gate the entire client CardGrid behavior on `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_FLIP_TAG_FILTER === '1'` — when off, fall back to the existing server-render path so a regression can ship dark. /tag/[slug] is OUT of scope (it's a separate route segment; the flipBridge does not span across route segment changes cleanly because both the page shell and the grid unmount).
tasks.githubIssueBody:
## What
GSAP Flip-based reflow on /search and /browse when the tag filter changes — cards slide from old slot to new slot, leavers fade out absolutely, enterers fade+scale in.

## Why
Demo: https://demos.gsap.com/demo/flexbox-filtering/ — but the demo runs entirely client-side. Our /search and /browse are server components, so the verbatim pattern can't survive a `router.push`.

## Architecture (committed)

**Module-level FlipBridge** (`frontend/lib/flipBridge.ts`):
- `snapshot(items)` → stores `Flip.getState(items, { props: 'opacity,transform' })` plus a key (pathname + prev tagIds)
- `consume()` → returns the state and clears it (one-shot)
- `clear()` → for HMR / Fast Refresh
- Flip states hold cloned rects, not live node refs, so they survive the unmount/remount across navigation

**Suspense**: CardGrid becomes a client component that reads `useSearchParams`. Wrap its callsites with `<Suspense fallback={<CardGrid.Skeleton />}>` in `frontend/app/search/page.tsx` and `frontend/app/browse/page.tsx` (Next.js requirement when calling `useSearchParams` in a child of a server page).

**Card identity**: every card root carries `data-flip-id={`${type}:${id}`}` so Flip can match across the navigation. Required on StoryCard, SeriesCard, ContinueCard.

**ContinueCard / ContinueReadingRow** are in scope — `/search` results can include continue-reading rows and they also need `data-flip-id`.

**Flip options** (committed):
```
Flip.from(state, {
  duration: 0.55,
  ease: 'power2.out',
  absolute: true,    // leavers go position:absolute so survivors don't fight reflow
  simple: true,      // skip nested-element diffing — flat list of cards, faster
  stagger: { amount: 0.4 },  // total stagger budget, not per-item (handles 50+ cards)
  onEnter: els => gsap.fromTo(els, { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92 }, { opacity: 1, scale: 1, duration: 0.4 }),
  onLeave: els => gsap.to(els, { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92, duration: 0.3 }),
})
```

**Grid stability**: pin `gsap.set(container, { minHeight: container.offsetHeight })` at the start of the Flip and clear it `onComplete` so the parent doesn't shrink when leavers go absolute.

**Fast Refresh / HMR**: in `flipBridge.ts`,
```
if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && (module as any).hot) {
  (module as any).hot.dispose(() => bridge.clear());
}
```
Document in code comment that this is the legacy Webpack HMR API; under Turbopack use `import.meta.webpackHot?.dispose?.(() => bridge.clear())`.

**Feature flag**: gate the whole client-side CardGrid behavior behind `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_FLIP_TAG_FILTER === '1'`. T5 has the most production risk, so it ships dark and is toggled per-environment.

## Out of scope
- `/tag/[slug]` — separate route segment, page shell unmounts, the flipBridge does not span it cleanly
- Reading-position carryover on the cards (unrelated)

## Cross-cutting note (read T4 first)
`frontend/lib/gsap.ts` needs to register Flip. Whichever of T4 / T5 lands first must consolidate plugin registration into one call: `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, ScrollToPlugin, Flip)`.

## Test plan
- [ ] /search, click a tag — cards reflow with Flip, no full-page navigation flash
- [ ] /browse, click a tag — same
- [ ] Click a tag that leaves only 2 results — leavers fade absolute, survivors slide to new flex slots
- [ ] Click All — all cards re-enter with onEnter fade+scale
- [ ] 50+ cards visible — total stagger stays under 0.5s (proves stagger.amount budget)
- [ ] Turn off `NEXT_PUBLIC_FLIP_TAG_FILTER` — falls back to existing server-render, no animation, no regression
- [ ] Hit /tag/[slug] from /search — full navigation, no Flip attempt (confirms out-of-scope)
- [ ] Trigger a Fast Refresh while a tag filter is mid-animation — no orphan bridge state, no Flip-on-stale-nodes error
- [ ] Toggle reduce-motion — Flip.from is replaced with `Flip.from(state, { duration: 0 })` so positions sync without animation
tasks.reducedMotionPlan: When `prefersReducedMotion()` is true, CardGrid still consumes the bridge state but calls `Flip.from(state, { duration: 0 })` so the layout syncs instantly with no transition — onEnter/onLeave become synchronous opacity sets. Stagger.amount drops to 0. The min-height pin happens but clears synchronously.
tasks.changesFromOriginal: Committed to the module-level flipBridge architecture (instead of leaving the choice between bridge/intercept-then-navigate/client-only-filter open). Explicitly added Suspense to filesToChange via frontend/app/search/page.tsx and frontend/app/browse/page.tsx — required because the new client CardGrid reads useSearchParams. Pinned `{ absolute: true, simple: true }` on Flip.from and added the grid container min-height pin. suggestedSequence.rationale: Ship smooth scroll restore first — smallest blast radius (one hook, one line replaced) and it touches frontend/lib/gsap.ts. Whichever of T4/T5 lands first MUST collapse plugin registration into a single `gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger, ...)` call rather than separate calls, because GSAP's registerPlugin accepts multiple args and a second call costs an unnecessary module evaluation.

Physics-based button feedback next — independent of T4, no cross-cutting plugin registration concerns beyond Physics2DPlugin/CustomBounce/CustomEase additions (multi-arg registerPlugin call established by T4). High user-visible win, low coupling.
Admin NoteCard Flip — adds Flip to the registerPlugin call. Lower production risk than T5 because admin-only. Validates the Flip integration before we expose it to public traffic in T5.

Magnetic dock — depends on the CSS hover-transform removals being correct, and benefits from being applied AFTER T2 sets the overwrite:'auto' pattern that lets multiple GSAP writers share a transform. Touches the most React components (hero, CardGrid, ContinueReadingRow, ChapterList) but no new plugin registration.

Ship last — feature-flagged behind `NEXT_PUBLIC_FLIP_TAG_FILTER`. Highest risk (server→client conversion of CardGrid, Suspense additions, flipBridge module-state). By landing after T1, the cards already have stable refs and overwrite:'auto' on transform writes; the Flip reflow won't fight the dock hover.

openQuestions: Particle z-index for T3's Like burst: should the spans render fixed-position z:9999 over the entire viewport (current spec), or be appended inside the LikeButton wrapper so they're clipped by overflow:hidden on the reading view? The wrapper approach is safer for stacked modals but eats the burst on small buttons.

T5 stagger budget: 0.4s total feels right at 30+ cards, but on a sparse /search result (3 cards) a 0.4 budget means 0.13s per card and reads as too snappy. Should the stagger be a function like `{ each: 0.08, from: 'start', amount: undefined }` clamped at 0.4 max, or stay as a fixed `amount: 0.4` and accept the snappy small-set feel?

T2 autosave-on-collapsed-card guard: should a collapsed card's textarea ALSO save on blur (the current behavior — guard only blocks the always-mounted-but-collapsed branch's debounce timer), or does blur-save on collapsed cards need an explicit `if (expanded)` block too?
